step_description: Remediate MAI-1 (Maintainability file-size budget) by splitting oversized non-test Go files so every tracked non-test .go file is <= 1500 lines, then refresh Hypergenium verifier evidence.
prompt_text:
You are a remediation agent executing the next Hypergenium roadmap step for this repo.

Context (source of truth)
- Roadmap: hgm-infra/planning/lift-10of10-roadmap.md (Rubric v0.1.0)
- Rubric: hgm-infra/planning/lift-10of10-rubric.md
- Evidence plan: hgm-infra/planning/lift-evidence-plan.md
- Deterministic verifier entrypoint: bash ./hgm-infra/verifiers/hgm-verify-rubric.sh
- Current rubric report: hgm-infra/evidence/hgm-rubric-report.json
- Current failing rubric item: MAI-1 (file budget check)
  - Evidence: hgm-infra/evidence/MAI-1-output.log
  - Expected failure mode: one or more non-test Go files exceed the 1500-line budget

Why this is the next step
- The current rubric report has exactly one FAIL (MAI-1). Most other non-doc gaps are BLOCKED by missing verifiers (future milestones).
- Fixing MAI-1 removes the only FAIL and should move the overall rubric status toward BLOCKED (i.e., remaining work is known and explicitly tracked).

Goal
- Fix ONLY rubric item MAI-1 by ensuring there are no file budget violations.
- Concretely: after remediation, running bash ./hgm-infra/verifiers/hgm-verify-rubric.sh must report MAI-1 as PASS, and MAI-1-output.log must not list any violations.
- Keep changes behavior-preserving (refactor/split only) and keep all other currently-passing rubric items passing (no regressions).

Strict guardrails (anti-drift)
- Do NOT change the MAI-1 budget policy (do not raise the limit, do not add allowlists/exceptions, do not change the verifier).
- Do NOT move production logic into *_test.go files or generated files to

lines; that is budget dilution.
- Do NOT change go.mod/go.sum (root or example modules) unless you can prove a module graph break was introduced by this step (normally not needed for file splitting).
- Do NOT change .golangci.yml or CI/workflow files (.github/workflows/*).
- Do NOT attempt to implement missing TODO verifiers (MAI-2/MAI-3, QUA-2, etc.) in this step.
- Keep the refactor mechanical and reviewable: splitting files and moving code within the same package is expected; semantic changes are not.

Allowed write locations (explicitly allowed for this step)
- You MAY modify/create Go source files under the existing packages implicated by MAI-1 violations (e.g., pkg/**).
- You MUST write progress notes and any additional evidence only under hgm-infra/evidence/.

Procedure
1) Confirm baseline failure (required)
   - Run: bash ./hgm-infra/verifiers/hgm-verify-rubric.sh
   - Confirm MAI-1 is FAIL in: hgm-infra/evidence/hgm-rubric-report.json
   - Inspect: hgm-infra/evidence/MAI-1-output.log
     Record the violating files and their line counts.

2) For each violating file, split into smaller files within the same package
   General approach (safe, Go-idiomatic, and behavior-preserving):
   - Keep the package name the same (e.g., package lift / package cli / package testing).
   - Create new files in the same directory/package, moving related blocks (types, helpers, subcomponents) into their own file(s).
   - Prefer splitting by responsibility and cohesion. Examples (choose names that match the file content):
     - app.go -> app_core.go, app_routes.go, app_events.go, app_websocket.go
     - dynamorm_commands.go -> dynamorm_scaffold.go, dynamorm_migrate.go, dynamorm_helpers.go
     - types.go -> types_severity.go, types_reports.go, types_validation.go
     - mocks.go -> mocks_dynamorm.go, mocks_clients.go, mocks_helpers.go
   - Keep exported identifiers (types/functions) unchanged unless absolutely necessary.
   - Keep comments close to their declarations (especially for exported symbols).
   - After each split, run gofmt on touched files.

   Practical tips (to stay safe and avoid accidental behavior change):
   - Prefer “move” over “rewrite”. Avoid reformatting unrelated sections.
   - Avoid changing function bodies unless required to resolve compile errors after moving code.
   - If a moved function relies on file-level init or variables, move those along with it.
   - Keep the build free of circular imports: splitting within a package does not introduce imports, so this should be safe.

3) Local verification while you work (recommended)
   - As you finish each package split, run at least a compile check for the repo:
     - go test -run TestNonexistent -count=0 ./...
   - If you introduce compile errors, fix them immediately (still within the same package / same refactor intent).

4) Final verification and evidence refresh (required)
   - Run: bash ./hgm-infra/verifiers/hgm-verify-rubric.sh
   - Confirm in hgm-infra/evidence/hgm-rubric-report.json:
     - MAI-1 status is PASS
   - Confirm hgm-infra/evidence/MAI-1-output.log indicates no violations (or is a success message).
   - Check that previously PASS items (e.g., QUA-1, CON-1, CON-2, COM-1, SEC-1, DOC-4, DOC-5) remain PASS.

5) Record progress (required)
   - Create: hgm-infra/evidence/roadmap-progress-M3-MAI-1.md
   - Include:
     - Date/time
     - Baseline violations (copy the list from the baseline MAI-1-output.log)
     - What files you split, and the new file names created
     - A brief statement that changes were refactor-only (no intended behavior changes)
     - Final verifier summary (PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED counts) with pointers to:
       - hgm-infra/evidence/hgm-rubric-report.json
       - hgm-infra/evidence/MAI-1-output.log

Acceptance criteria
- MAI-1 is PASS in hgm-infra/evidence/hgm-rubric-report.json
- No non-test tracked .go files exceed 1500 lines (as enforced by the verifier).
- Repo still builds/tests (at minimum, go test ./... succeeds; ideally make test succeeds).

If you get blocked
- If you cannot reduce a file below 1500 lines without a risky refactor, STOP before changing behavior.
- Document the constraint in roadmap-progress-M3-MAI-1.md, including:
  - which file
  - why splitting is non-trivial
  - what minimal next step you propose (e.g., extracting a subcomponent behind an internal interface)
- Do not add allowlists or raise limits as a workaround.
expected_outputs: pkg/** (one or more files modified/created to split oversized files and meet the 1500-line budget)
guardrails: Do not change verifier policy (no allowlists, no raised limits)
Do not move production logic into tests/generated files to evade budgets
Do not change go.mod/go.sum unless strictly necessary for compilation (not expected)
Make only refactor/splitting changes needed for MAI-1; avoid unrelated behavior changes
